scenes.description: A view of Queensway Quay in Gibraltar from the early 19th century, showcasing the bustling maritime activity and strategic importance of the harbor during this period.

highlights.title: Commercial Wharf and Stone Buildings
highlights.text: The busy stone wharf is lined with multi-story warehouses and packed with cargo barrels, featuring an early manual crane for loading vessels.

highlights.title: Rigged Merchant and Naval Vessels
highlights.text: A large, fully-rigged three-masted ship is docked directly at the quay, while multiple square-rigged vessels sit anchored across the calm harbor.

highlights.title: Distant Breakwater and Coastline
highlights.text: A long, protective breakwater mole with a small navigation marker stretches across the mid-ground against the distant backdrop of the Spanish mountains.

scenes.description: Modern shipping, naval operations, and industrial harbor infrastructure at Queensway Quay in the mid-20th century, reflecting the continued strategic and commercial significance of Gibraltar's port facilities.

highlights.title: Industrial Wharves and Portal Cranes
highlights.text: Large corrugated metal cargo sheds and industrial motorized portal cranes line the concrete quay, illustrating twentieth-century cargo-handling efficiency.

highlights.title: Harbor Tugboats and Barges
highlights.text: An active tugboat maneuvers a heavy cargo barge through the harbor basin, while another tug operates nearby to assist larger vessels.

highlights.title: Naval Escort and Merchant Fleet
highlights.text: A modern grey naval frigate sits anchored in the harbor alongside large commercial cargo ships and tankers, highlighting the port's dual strategic and economic role.

highlights.title: Historical Fortifications and Ramparts
highlights.text: The massive, stone-hewn defensive walls and bastions of Gibraltar's historic fortifications loom directly behind the modernized port facilities.
